newsitem.title: USA: Questions raised about phone interceptors.
newsitem.headline: Questions raised about phone interceptors.

text.p: The chairman of the House Commerce Committee asked Wednesday for an inquiry into whether scanning devices like that used to eavesdrop on Speaker Newt Gingrich's telephone conversation violated federal laws.

Representative Thomas Bliley in a letter also asked the Federal Communications Commission to investigate whether anyone connected with the Gingrich eavesdropping broke federal law and FCC regulations.

A Florida couple said this week that they monitored and taped a conversation between Gingirch and his top lieutenants about his ethics case, using a police scanner that they had bought from an electronics store.
In a statement Bliley cited published reports that the store had told the couple, John and Alice Martin, that the device could not receive cellular phone channels.

"Either the Martins illegally altered the device, or the wiretapping incident din't happen as accidentally as they led us to believe," Bliley said. "Either way, it is incumbent on the FCC to investigate."
